text: The pipeline begins with the input referring expression describing specific target attributes.
Simultaneously, the query image containing multiple candidate objects is provided.
Both inputs pass through dedicated backbones and a cross-modality feature enhancer.
This extracts multi-scale visual features across four pyramid levels.
The visual features are projected via a linear mapping layer into the text feature space.
Meanwhile, the aligned text feature is retrieved from the language branch.
Element-wise multiplication computes cross-modal correlation between mapped visual tokens and text.
This generates similarity features responsive to the specified referring expression.
A U-shaped Contextual Attribute Density Estimator processes the similarity and visual features.
The estimator outputs predicted density maps indicating attribute intensity.
These are compared against the ground truth density maps.
The density loss provides direct supervision to guide fine-grained contextual attribute learning.
The intermediate multi-scale representations form the Contextual Attribute Density features.
Next, the CAD Attention Module applies spatial attention to enhance foreground regions.
The multi-scale CAD features enter the spatial attention branch.
Channel-wise max pooling extracts peak activation features.
Average pooling simultaneously aggregates channel context.
The pooled descriptors are concatenated along the channel dimension.
A convolutional layer processes the combined spatial descriptor.
A sigmoid function produces the spatial attention map.
Processing continues into the channel attention block.
The raw visual features are introduced.
They are multiplied by the spatial attention map to yield spatially attended features.
Spatial max pooling aggregates peak activations across spatial dimensions.
Spatial average pooling captures global context across each channel.
Shared multilayer perceptrons transform both pooled representations.
The transformed channel vectors are summed together.
A sigmoid function generates the final channel attention weights.
These weights are applied element-wise to the spatially attended visual features.
This produces the CAD-enhanced multi-scale visual features.
In parallel, the CAD Dynamic Query Module initializes the object queries.
The CAD features provide rich spatial and attribute density information.
Top-K positions with highest text similarity scores are selected as key locations.
For content initialization, the text init branch dynamically encodes expression attributes.
The text feature is passed into a learnable linear layer.
A GELU activation generates dynamic text features.
Initial query embeddings are introduced.
Matrix multiplication combines queries with dynamic text features to form text weights.
A second multiplication with the text feature yields text-dynamic initialized queries.
Cross-attention then fuses these text-initialized queries with the top-K CAD features.
This creates highly discriminative dynamic queries tailored to both image density and text.
The CAD-enhanced visual features and dynamic text queries are gathered together.
They are fed into the cross-modality localization decoder across successive decoding layers.
The decoder outputs accurate bounding box predictions and referring expression counts.
Finally, the localization loss optimizes overall detection and counting performance.
